flawed_step: Lines 1 and 7 assert that every real semi-inner product space is automatically a complex semi-inner product space.
counterexample: Take V=R with ⟨x,y⟩=xy. This is a real inner product space, hence a real semi-inner product space. It is not automatically a complex vector space: if multiplication by i were compatible with its usual real scalar multiplication, write i·1=a∈R. Then i·a=a(i·1)=a², while i·(i·1)=−1, forcing a²=−1, impossible for real a. Thus this structure is not a complex semi-inner product space.
assessment_summary: The claimed implication fails because a real semi-inner product space need not possess the complex scalar multiplication required of a complex semi-inner product space.
